newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares finish weaker, blue chips above 1000.
newsitem.headline: KL shares finish weaker, blue chips above 1000.

text.p: Sellers continued to nudge Kuala Lumpur share prices lower, with blue chips hovering above the psychological 1,000 level at the close.

Uncertainty spawned by a sharply weaker ringgit and rocketing interest rates kept interest low, analysts said. "I don't think you'll see much buying coming back soon," said an equity analyst at a local brokerage firm.

At the close, the Composite Index of 100 blue chips ended down 8.39 points or 0.83 percent to 1,004.09. It sank as low as 1,002.29 earlier. The Second Board index eased 3.89 points or 0.73 percent to 526.63.
"I'm actually a little surprised," said Christopher Podbury, chief operating officer of HA Options and Financial Futures. "I thought the market would be picking up by now."
But, he added, "They (investors) are still not completely convinced speculators are out of the (ringgit) market and everything is hunky-dory."

Central Bank Negara checked dollar/ringgit rates at 2.57 in late afternoon trading. The Malaysian currency has been sinking since Monday, and hit a 33-month low yesterday. The benchmark three-month KLIBOR rate was fixed at 10.3 percent at 0300 GMT on Wednesday. It was quoted as high as 15 percent this week.
Volume topped 215 million shares, with losers leading gainers by 351 to 237.

A handful of finance stocks were actively traded. Higher interest rates are a negative factor for this sector due to higher financing costs. MBF Capital fell six cents to 3.92 ringgit, RHB Capital shed 60 cents to 7.00 and Affin Holdings eased 25 to 5.45.
"If you are a financial institution that's a net borrower of interbank funds, you're likely to be badly hit," an equity analyst said.
Weaker blue chips included Telekom, off 20 cents to 10.80 ringgit, Tenaga, down 20 to 10.80 and Genting, down 40 to 11.40.
Financial markets in Malaysia are closed on Thursday for observance of Prophet Muhammad's birthday.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot July contract lost 3.1 points to 994.0 with 1,155 lots traded. August futures shed 5.0 points to 994.0 with 54 lots having changed hands.
